{{Short description|2011 film score by various artists}} {{EngvarB|date=September 2013}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}} {{Infobox album | name = Ra.One | type = Soundtrack | artist = [[Vishal–Shekhar]] | cover = RaOnealbum.jpg | alt = | released = 21 September 2011 | recorded = 2010–2011 | venue = | studio = YRF Studios, [[Mumbai]]
[[City of Prague Philharmonic Orchestra|Smečky Music Studios]], Prague | genre = [[Film soundtrack|Feature film soundtrack]] | length = 59:21 | language = Hindi | label = [[T-Series (company)|T-Series]] | producer = * Vishal–Shekhar * Abhijit Nalani * Abhijit Vaghani * Giorgio Tuinfort * John Stewart | prev_title = [[Rascals (2011 film)|Rascals]] | prev_year = 2011 | next_title = [[The Dirty Picture]] | next_year = 2011 }} '''''Ra.One''''' is the [[soundtrack album]] composed by the duo [[Vishal–Shekhar]], to the 2011 [[Indian cinema|Indian]] [[superhero film]] [[Ra.One|of the same name]], written and directed by [[Anubhav Sinha]], and starring [[Shah Rukh Khan|Shahrukh Khan]], [[Kareena Kapoor]], [[Armaan Verma]] and [[Arjun Rampal]] in the lead roles. It also stars [[Shahana Goswami]], [[Dalip Tahil]] and Chinese-british actor [[Tom Wu]] in supporting roles, along with [[Rajinikanth]], [[Sanjay Dutt]] and [[Priyanka Chopra]] making cameo appearances. The film is jointly produced by [[Eros International]] and Khan's production company, [[Red Chillies Entertainment]],{{cite news|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/SRK-on---Ra-1------Don-2---and-Yash-Chopra--s-next/574434|author=Bollywood Hungama News Network|title=SRK on 'Ra-1', 'Don 2' and Yash Chopra's next|date=2 February 2010|work=[[The Indian Express]]|access-date=11 February 2010}} and was originally scheduled to release on 3 June 2011. However, due to extensive post-production work involving special effects and the [[Stereoscopy|3D]] conversion, its release was postponed, and saw a worldwide opening during the [[Diwali|Diwali weekend]] of 26 October 2011.{{cite web|url=http://www.businessofcinema.com/news.php?newsid=17286|title=Shah Rukh Khan's Ra.One postponed to Diwali 2011|date=17 November 2010|work=BusinessofCinema|access-date=17 November 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101120102855/http://businessofcinema.com/news.php?newsid=17286|archive-date=20 November 2010}} The album features fifteen tracks, and was released on 21 September 2011 by [[T-Series (company)|T-Series]]. ==Production== The soundtrack of ''Ra.One'' was composed by [[Vishal–Shekhar]] whilst the lyrics were penned by Atahar Panchi, Vishal Dadlani, [[Kumaar]], [[Anubhav Sinha]] and [[Anvita Dutt Guptan]]. In addition to composing the film's soundtrack, the music directors brought together the 200-piece [[Prague Philharmonic Orchestra]] to record the film's background score. They said, "Shahrukh and Anubhav wanted a particular sound and we have managed to bring it alive for [the film]."{{cite news|url=http://www.asianage.com/bollywood/raone-s-music-goes-places-257|author=Tuteja, Joginder|title=Ra.One's music goes places|date=5 September 2011|work=[[Asian Age]]|access-date=7 September 2010}} Director Anubhav Sinha announced that the soundtrack would also feature two songs recorded by [[Senegalese American]] [[R&B]] singer [[Akon]].{{cite news|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/akon-records-a-song-for-shah-rukhs-ra.one/589138/|author=Express News Service|title=Akon in city, lends voice to SRK's Ra.1|date=9 March 2010|work=The Indian Express|access-date=22 August 2010}} It is said that [[Shah Rukh Khan|Shahrukh Khan]] met the singer in New York and became his "big fan", then he asked him to fly down to India to record a song for the film.{{cite news | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/news-interviews/Kareena-marries-Akon-SRK/articleshow/5663747.cms | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120928085645/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2010-03-10/news-interviews/28128252_1_akon-shahrukh-superhero | url-status=live | archive-date=28 September 2012 | title=Kareena marries Akon, SRK! | access-date=23 September 2011 | work=[[The Times of India]] | date=10 March 2010}} Akon arrived to [[Mumbai]] in March 2010 for two days to record both the songs ''Chammak Challo'' and ''Criminal''.{{cite web|url=http://www.filmfare.com/articles/akon-to-sing-for-srk-for-free-552.html|title=Akon in India for Ra.One|work=[[Filmfare]]|access-date=21 September 2011}} Shahrukh Khan, [[Kareena Kapoor]] and Ra.One director Anubhav Sinha held a press conference to declare the association of the [[Grammy Award]] winning singer with the film.{{cite web|url=http://videos.oneindia.in/watch/18038/shahrukh-kareena-welcome-akon.html|title=SRK welcomes Akon|work=Oneindia|access-date=21 September 2011|archive-date=29 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120329233854/http://videos.oneindia.in/watch/18038/shahrukh-kareena-welcome-akon.html|url-status=dead}} The song ''Chammak Challo'' was co-composed by Akon and was recorded at the Yash Raj Studios. The makers of the film have complied with international copyright laws and have obtained the license to use [[Ben E. King]]'s song, "''[[Stand by Me (Ben E. King song)|Stand By Me]]''", on which they have based the song "''Dildaara''".{{cite web|url=http://movies.ndtv.com/movie_story.aspx?ID=ENTEN20110184255&keyword=music&subcatg=MUSICINDIA&nid=134111|agency=Indo-Asian News Service|author-link=Indo-Asian News Service|title=Music Review: SRK's Ra.One|work=[[NDTV]]|publisher=Prannoy Roy Publications|date=16 September 2011|access-date=16 September 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110923150631/http://movies.ndtv.com/movie_story.aspx?ID=ENTEN20110184255&keyword=music&subcatg=MUSICINDIA&nid=134111|archive-date=23 September 2011}} The song ''Jiya Mora Ghabraaye'' was originally composed as an instrumental piece as a part of the background score, but due to great appreciation from the production team, it was eventually converted into an original track and added to the album. Music producer, [[Abhijit Vaghani]] stated: "Our mindset was in the zone of all superhero movies for the score (...) I've taken my engineers in my car along with a mike and recorded sounds from inside my car. The point of this was, one of the pieces, which was the 'chase' sequence was so loved by all that it eventually got converted into a track called 'Jiya Mora'. I also added the 'dub step' in the middle of the track."{{cite web|url=http://www.bollywoodhungama.com/features/2011/10/12/8009/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111014232619/http://www.bollywoodhungama.com/features/2011/10/12/8009/|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 October 2011|author=Patel, Devansh |title=SRK loved the score of Ra.One immensely|work=[[Bollywood Hungama]]|date=12 October 2011|access-date=16 October 2011}} Vaghani also revealed that they have created a Spanish piece which he has sung in as well, it consists of an interaction scene between the two people. They have also called a Spanish translator to come up with the lyrics. The piece however, was not included in the soundtrack. Music rights was bought by T-Series for a record sum of {{INRConvert|150|m}}.{{cite web|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/ra.one-rakes-in-moolah-even-before-release/849345/3|work=[[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]]|location=India|title=Ra.One rakes in moolah even before release|date=21 September 2011|access-date=21 September 2011}} ==Release== [[File:Ra.One audio news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/Shah-Rukh-Khan-sues-a-jewellery-brand/Article1-734627.aspx|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125184553/http://www.hindustantimes.com/Shah-Rukh-Khan-sues-a-jewellery-brand/Article1-734627.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 illegally using the unreleased song at the India International Jewellery Week 2011, asking for a compensation of {{Indian Rupee}} 20 million. The film's music launch took place in a huge set at Mumbai's [[Film City, Mumbai|Film City]] where performances were seen by the film's music directors and cast members. The star studded event's telecast rights were sold to a TV channel for {{INRConvert|100|m}}.{{cite news | url=http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2011-09-25/news-interviews/30200118_1_srk-s-red-chillies-shah-rukh-khan-anubhav-sinha/3 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120710143529/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2011-09-25/news-interviews/30200118_1_srk-s-red-chillies-shah-rukh-khan-anubhav-sinha/3 | url-status=dead | archive-date=10 July 2012 | title=Ra.One challenges Shah Rukh Khan, the star | date=25 September 2011 | work=[[The Times of India]] | access-date=26 September 2011}} [[Radio Mirchi]] ran a contest through which it gave its listeners a chance to not only attend the music launch event but also meet the stars of the film.{{cite web|author=RnM Team|date=22 September 2011|title=Mirchi listeners meet their superhero!|url=http://www.radioandmusic.com/content/editorial/news-releases/mirchi-listeners-meet-their-superhero|access-date=22 September 2011|work=[[Radio Mirchi]]}} The [[Tamil language|Tamil]] version of the audio was released in Satyam Cinemas, [[Chennai]] on 5 October 2011. Shahrukh Khan along with [[Mani Ratnam]], [[Suhasini Maniratnam]], [[Santosh Sivan]], [[Soundarya Rajinikanth]] and Abirami Ramanathan were present in the occasion.{{cite web|date=6 October 2011|title=Ra.One's Tamil version audio launched|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/video/entertainment/20/ra.ones-tamil-version-audio-launched/6309|access-date=6 October 2011|work=The New Indian Express}}{{cite web|date=5 October 2011|title='Ra.One' audio launch in Chennai – An entertaining affair|url=http://www.indiaglitz.com/channels/hindi/article/71871.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011124855/http://www.indiaglitz.com/channels/hindi/article/71871.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 October 2011|access-date=6 October 2011|work=IndiaGlitz}} The songs of the film have also been dubbed in Telugu, which was released on 9 October 2011. The lyrics for the Tamil version have been penned by [[Vairamuthu]] while the lyrics for the Telugu version have been penned by [[Vanamali]], Rajshri Sudhakar and [[Bhuvana Chandra|Bhuvanachandra]]. Both the versions of the album have been met by a huge positive response from the audience in south India.{{cite web|title=Ra.One songs take Tamil listeners by storm|url=https://www.filmibeat.com/tamil/news/2011/ra-one-songs-take-tamil-listeners-storm-121011.html|access-date=8 October 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130108071542/http://entertainment.oneindia.in/tamil/news/2011/ra-one-songs-take-tamil-listeners-storm-121011.html|archive-date=8 January 2013}} Due to the extremely positive response for the album, especially the song ''Chammak challo'', Akon decided to branch out and make tracks especially for [[Bollywood]] projects and now wants to have a [[Rediff.com]] | rev4Score = {{Rating|3.5|5}} | }} ===Critical reception=== Upon release, the album was met by overwhelmingly positive reviews from critics. Joginder Tuteja from [[Bollywood Hungama]] gave it 4.5 out of 5 stars, concluding: "''Ra.One'' has brilliancy written all over it and is clearly a huge winner all the way. It isn't just the grandest score of the year but is also one of the hugest ever that has come out of Bollywood. Music here not just meets the huge expectations but also surpasses it at various junctures, hence making it a satiating experience for the listener. A definite choice of the season."{{cite web|author=Tuteja, Joginder|date=23 September 2011|title=Ra.One: Music Review|url=http://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movies/musicreview/14208/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100108022110/http://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movies/musicreview/14208/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 January 2010|access-date=1 October 2011|work=Bollywood Hungama}} According to Devesh Sharma from ''[[Filmfare]]'', who gave the music a rating of 5 stars from 5, the album is "worth every penny!" further adding: "A truly international album for a truly international film. The orchestration, programming and vocals fuse together to make it a truly world class album. Vishal–Shekhar have raised the bar and Ra.One would be a tough act to follow, not only for them but for others as well."{{cite web|title=Ra.1 Music worth every penny|url=http://www.filmfare.com/articles/raone-2774.html|access-date=1 October 2011|work=[[Filmfare]]}} [[Indo-Asian News Service]] rated the album favourably and said: "To cut a long story short, the album delivers big-time as composer duo Vishal-Shekhar pack a killer punch. ''Ra.One'', therefore, lives up to expectations and perhaps even surpasses some. It's more than worth it, it's a winner all the way."{{cite web|agency=Indo-Asian News Service|author-link=Indo-Asian News Service|date=25 September 2011|title=Music Review: SRK's Ra.One|url=http://movies.ndtv.com/movie_story.aspx?ID=ENTEN20110184255&keyword=music&subcatg=MUSICINDIA&nid=134111|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110923150631/http://movies.ndtv.com/movie_story.aspx?ID=ENTEN20110184255&keyword=music&subcatg=MUSICINDIA&nid=134111|archive-date=23 September 2011|access-date=1 October 2011|work=[[NDTV]]|publisher=Prannoy Roy Publications}} ''[[The Times of India]]'' gave it a thumbs up and added: "The album of the film lives up to the expectations, thanks to composers Vishal-Shekhar for packing a musical punch for the sci-fi movie. The album is worth buying and offers some interesting and entertaining tracks. Kudos to the music composers!"{{cite news|author=Kher, Ruchika|date=26 September 2011|title=Ra.One|work=The Times of India|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/music/music-reviews/RA-One/articleshow/10005520.cms|access-date=1 October 2011}} The ''[[Hindustan Times]]'' gave the album 3.5 stars from 5 and elaborating: "Shahrukh Khan's RA.One has been generating curiosity since beginning and expectations have been high from its music as well. The album of the film lives up to the expectations, thanks to composers Vishal-Shekhar for packing a musical punch for the sci-fi movie (..) On the whole the album is worth buying and offers some interesting and entertaining tracks. Kudos to the music composers!"{{cite web|title=Ra.1 M.R|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/Thumbs-up-to-RA-One-s-music/Article1-746348.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110923183352/http://www.hindustantimes.com/Thumbs-up-to-RA-One-s-music/Article1-746348.aspx|archive-date=23 September 2011|access-date=1 October 2011|work=Hindustan Times}} [[Sukanya Verma]] from [[Rediff.com]] gave it 3.5 stars and noted: "Vishal-Shekhar eventually succeed in emulating that all-important larger-than-life appeal. There's no denying this. ''Ra.One'', with all its pomp and pizzazz, is a thoroughly enjoyable soundtrack. It's grand. It's great. It's, well, give it a shot."{{cite web|author=Verma, Sukanya|date=21 September 2011|title=Review: Ra.One songs are a great extract:
Ra.One is the soundtrack album composed by the duo Vishal–Shekhar, to the 2011 Indian superhero film of the same name, written and directed by Anubhav Sinha, and starring Shahrukh Khan, Kareena Kapoor, Armaan Verma and Arjun Rampal in the lead roles. It also stars Shahana Goswami, Dalip Tahil and Chinese-british actor Tom Wu in supporting roles, along with Rajinikanth, Sanjay Dutt and Priyanka Chopra making cameo appearances.
The film is jointly produced by Eros International and Khan's production company, Red Chillies Entertainment, and was originally scheduled to release on 3 June 2011. However, due to extensive post-production work involving special effects and the 3D conversion, its release was postponed, and saw a worldwide opening during the Diwali weekend of 26 October 2011. The album features fifteen tracks, and was released on 21 September 2011 by T-Series.
